symptom: TypeScript validation failed because an estimate row handler used a mutation status type without importing it.
rootCause: The handler was updated to preserve local row state by mutation status, but the new status type was not imported from the mutation hook.
fixSummary: Imported EstimateRowMutationStatus alongside the existing mutation map types.

symptom: Runtime API and email error paths bypassed the structured logger with raw console.error
rootCause: The static error-handling gate covered empty catches but not raw runtime console.error in API and email code
fixSummary: Extended the gate and converted API and email console.error sites to logAppError or emitLogRecord with safe context
validation: bun run test:dom focused error logging suite

symptom: Vitest structured logger calls wrote synthetic route and email errors into the default local developer log, making agent debugging snapshots look like current runtime failures.
rootCause: The logger wrote to logs/dev.ndjson whenever NODE_ENV was not production, so NODE_ENV=test route and email tests polluted the developer runtime log unless each test manually disabled logging.
fixSummary: Default log-file writes are disabled in NODE_ENV=test unless ARCHESTIMATOR_DEV_LOG_PATH is explicit; logger tests use temp paths for intentional file-output checks.
validation: logs/dev.ndjson stayed 1255756 bytes before and after focused test suite

symptom: Runtime user and operator paths outside API and email could still bypass structured logging with raw console.error, weakening local NDJSON logs and agent debugging snapshots.
rootCause: The static error-handling gate originally rejected raw console.error only in API and email files, leaving public share deferred telemetry, component-library action errors, account audit failures, retention pass failures, and upload operations dashboard failures outside the structured logger invariant.
fixSummary: Converted those runtime surfaces to logAppError or emitLogRecord with safe context, and expanded validate:error-handling to reject raw console.error across the covered runtime user/operator paths.

symptom: Workers Logs proof collection required a request id before wrangler tail could observe the hosted request
rootCause: The collector searched for a pre-known request id, which made hosted proof collection manual and race-prone for new proof requests.
fixSummary: Added a protected observability proof route and marker-mode collector that tails by proof id while triggering the hosted route.

symptom: Cloudflare Worker readiness could pass manifest checks even if the hosted observability proof route was accidentally unwired
rootCause: The Cloudflare Worker readiness checker verified manifests and env names but did not inspect Worker source wiring for the protected observability proof route.
fixSummary: Added a non-secret workerProofRoutes source-contract group to cf:check-readiness covering protected proof routing, observability proof dispatch, CRON_SECRET auth, structured marker logging, and worker.dev proof-route preservation.

symptom: Agent debugging snapshot did not expose the latest local error recurrence key when there was no prior ledger match
rootCause: The recurrence ledger could match repeated errors, but new local error fingerprints were only implicit unless agents recomputed the key from route, event, class, and code.
fixSummary: Added debuggingLedger.latestErrorRecurrenceKey to the snapshot and recommended using it in the post-fix ops:debug-ledger record so future agents recognize the same fingerprint.

symptom: Alert scenario ownership and poller proof expectations were plan prose rather than an agent-checkable launch contract.
rootCause: The observability alert proof plan enumerated S-01 through S-07, but the debugging snapshot and readiness scripts did not expose scenario owners, channels, latency targets, proof commands, artifacts, or planned proof-producer blockers as structured data.
fixSummary: Added a typed alert scenario catalog, fail-closed readiness checker, package scripts, snapshot integration, tests, and protocol/state documentation so agents can distinguish local catalog readiness from production alert launch readiness.
validation: bun run ops:check-alert-scenarios exits 1 as expected until S-04/S-05/S-07 proof producers exist

symptom: Alert scenario catalog covered S-04 S-05 and S-07 in prose but left their proof producers planned.
rootCause: The hosted alert-delivery proof runner and production proof checker only modeled uptime error-rate and incident-escalation scenarios.
fixSummary: Extended the shared alert-delivery proof runner production checker drill catalog and agent snapshot tests to cover queue-dlq cron-failure and retention-failure as implemented proof producers.
followUps: Collect hosted Workers Logs plus six hosted alert-delivery artifacts with explicit production proof env gates.

symptom: Agent snapshot used production alert proof wording for a local proof-producer check.
rootCause: The alert scenario checker validated local catalog and producer availability but exposed readiness fields that could be mistaken for hosted delivery proof.
fixSummary: Renamed the alert scenario readiness fields and CLI output to productionAlertProducerReady and productionAlertScenarioProducerReady while keeping hosted delivery proof under productionHostedProofReady.
followUps: Keep local producer readiness and hosted proof readiness separate in future launch gates.

symptom: Hosted observability proof checker accepted valid-looking artifacts without confirming which local proof producer generated them.
rootCause: The Workers Logs and alert-delivery proof artifacts recorded hosted boundaries and redaction checks but did not include script/version producer metadata, so accidental hand-authored JSON could satisfy the bundle checker.
fixSummary: Added producer script/version metadata to the Workers Logs and alert-delivery proof artifacts and made ops:check-observability reject missing or unexpected producer metadata.
followUps: Collect hosted Workers Logs plus six hosted alert-delivery artifacts with explicit production proof env gates.

symptom: Agent handoffs showed hosted observability proof keys but hid per-artifact failed check labels.
rootCause: Snapshot and drill collapsed the production observability checker report to failed requirement keys, forcing agents to open separate proof reports to distinguish missing artifacts from stale or wrong-producer artifacts.
fixSummary: Surface compact redacted hostedProof.requirements diagnostics in agent snapshot and observability drill reports.
followUps: Collect real hosted Cloudflare Workers Logs and alert-delivery artifacts before claiming productionHostedProofReady.

symptom: Agent snapshots could present an old latest local error without saying whether the record was fresh enough to investigate.
rootCause: The local log snapshot summarized the latest error metadata but did not compute age or freshness, so agents could anchor on historical pre-fix records.
fixSummary: Add latest local error age and freshness metadata plus stale-record guidance to the agent debugging snapshot.
followUps: When freshness is stale, reproduce or observe a fresh local failure before changing product code.

symptom: Agent snapshot treated a Vitest-generated shared-link decision route diagnostic as the latest local app error.
rootCause: The snapshot summarized latest local error records without classifying nearby Vitest stack evidence, so diagnostic records emitted after route tests could masquerade as dev-app runtime failures.
fixSummary: Detect test-origin local errors from nearby route-error stack evidence and surface safe originEvidence in the agent snapshot.
followUps: Rerun route tests with temp ARCHESTIMATOR_DEV_LOG_PATH or reproduce in dev before treating origin:test logs as product bugs.

symptom: Direct logs:debug output still told agents to inspect a product route for a Vitest-generated shared-link decision diagnostic.
rootCause: The direct log explainer lacked the snapshot's test-origin classifier, so nearby route-error stack evidence was not used when explaining diagnostic records.
fixSummary: Teach tail-dev-logs to classify test-origin records from target and nearby stack evidence before emitting likely next steps.
followUps: If logs:debug reports test-origin evidence, rerun with temp ARCHESTIMATOR_DEV_LOG_PATH or reproduce in dev before changing product code.

symptom: Agent snapshots reported recurrence matches but did not summarize the latest prior status, fix, or validation before code changes.
rootCause: The recurrence ledger exposed recentMatches, but the snapshot next step made agents inspect the match array manually before knowing whether prior evidence was fixed, mitigated, observed, or still investigating.
fixSummary: Add debuggingLedger.latestErrorMatchSummary with status counts and latest match details, then make snapshot recommendations status-aware.

symptom: The production observability drill listed blocked and ready actions but did not group next steps by safe local checks versus hosted proof side effects.
rootCause: The drill exposed action statuses but lacked an execution-plan view that separated read-only commands from Cloudflare Logs tailing, synthetic alert delivery, and env/artifact blockers.
fixSummary: Add executionPlan.readOnlyReady, executionPlan.gatedExternalReady, and executionPlan.blocked groups plus a CLI runbook count line.

symptom: The agent debugging snapshot told agents to run the production observability drill but did not include the drill's read-only, gated-external, and blocked runbook buckets.
rootCause: The snapshot reused hosted proof env and artifact reports but did not project the drill execution plan into the primary agent handoff artifact.
fixSummary: Embed observabilityRunbook from the production observability drill execution plan and make snapshot recommendations point at blocked or gated hosted-proof steps.

symptom: The agent debugging snapshot summarized hosted proof and incident readiness but did not surface the first-user support monitoring readiness gate.
rootCause: Support monitoring readiness lived in launch:check-support-monitoring, so agents had to mentally join a separate command before knowing whether production support coverage was ready.
fixSummary: Embed sanitized supportMonitoring readiness and readiness.supportMonitoringReady in ops:agent-debug-snapshot without copying owner-label values.

symptom: Support monitoring readiness exposed only a flat missing list, forcing agents to infer whether blockers were operator confirmations, owner labels, or evidence artifact failures.
rootCause: The support readiness checker flattened all launch blockers into strings, so agent handoffs could not distinguish absent proof from present-but-failed incident or observability artifacts.
fixSummary: Emit structured support monitoring requirement diagnostics with summary counts, categories, statuses, sources, missing facts, and next actions; mirror them in the agent debug snapshot without owner-label values.

symptom: Agent snapshot latest local error can be a synthetic test diagnostic while the newest runtime-origin error is hidden behind it.
rootCause: The snapshot only surfaced the latest overall error and nearby test-origin classification did not account for diagnostic records adjacent to route-error stacks on bracketed Next.js dynamic paths.
fixSummary: Expose localLogs.latestRuntimeError, classify nearby same-route test stack evidence before or after the diagnostic record, and allow bracketed Next.js route paths while still rejecting query strings and fragments.

symptom: Next 16.2.10 dev server reached the V8 heap limit after idle Turbopack cache persistence and compaction.
rootCause: Next 16.2.10 retained Turbopack filesystem-cache state and performed persistence/compaction after requests. That idle work bypassed the request-finally memory restart check and exhausted the heap on an 8 GiB host.
fixSummary: Made bounded Webpack the default, retained cache-disabled memory-targeted Turbopack as an opt-in, enforced Node 22.12+/24.x before dev and typecheck, split Node-only instrumentation from Edge compilation, and gave TypeScript the measured 4 GiB heap budget.
validation: Cache-disabled Turbopack stress survived 13.5 minutes and three clean warm cycles across 25 routes; 93 samples, zero persistence/compaction/restarts, no Turbopack cache directory.
Node 24 default Webpack returned 200 for the exact incident route under the 2 GiB V8 ceiling.
Focused Vitest passed 4 files and 20 tests; targeted ESLint and validate:error-handling passed.
Node 24 typecheck passed with the scripted 4 GiB heap budget; Node 26 preflight exited cleanly before starting work.
followUps: Re-evaluate Turbopack default only after the retention/eviction fixes ship in a stable Next release and the same stress proof passes.

symptom: The default Next development command must use Turbopack without repeating the prior idle cache OOM.
rootCause: Next 16.2.10 persistent Turbopack filesystem-cache work exhausted the heap after requests; forcing Webpack avoided the crash but made the default developer loop unacceptably slow.
fixSummary: Restored explicit Turbopack as the default while retaining filesystem caching disabled, a 1.5 GiB Turbopack target, a 2 GiB V8 ceiling, supported-Node preflight, and Node/Edge instrumentation isolation; removed the irrelevant webpack-only experiment.
validation: TDD red-green: focused runtime-memory test failed on the webpack default, then passed after the Turbopack change.
bun dev reported Next.js 16.2.10 (Turbopack) and reached ready in 474-524 ms.
Authenticated five-cycle sweep across 11 public/workshop routes produced zero 5xx responses, 101-215 ms cycle averages, and 272-469 ms maxima.
The Turbopack filesystem-cache directory remained absent; .next/dev was 231 MiB and idle next-server RSS fell to 18 MiB.
Focused Vitest passed 2 files and 7 tests; targeted ESLint, type-check, and git diff --check passed.
followUps: Keep filesystem caching disabled until a newer stable Next release passes the same sustained route and idle-memory proof.
